newsitem.title: USA: No Fed action again, bill pass possible.
newsitem.headline: No Fed action again, bill pass possible.

text.p: The Federal Reserve will likely stay on the sidelines during its mid-morning intervention period Wednesday, but an outright purchase of bills this session is possible, analysts said.
With the first half of the two-week maintenance period ending Wednesday, analysts said operations in the past few sessions should take care of the day's small add need.
Federal funds were trading at their 5-1/4 percent target rate, offering little evidence of reserve pressures.
The Fed stayed out of the open market on Tuesday, given the four-day system RPs from Thursday still on the books.
Analysts said the 14-day system RPs from last week were another reason for the Fed to stay out of the market.

But the average daily add need rises dramatically in the second half of the maintenance period to above $6 billion, and then to above $7.5 billion in the next period, analysts said, likely forcing the Fed to add permanent reserves. An outright purchase of bills -- a bill pass -- seems likely as early as Wednesday, some predicted, although it seems more probable next week.
